title: Microsoft Teams Rooms on Android: redesigned on-device admin settings
summary: Hold: both automation cells say Microsoft has not documented a control, although Microsoft still publishes the device-configuration cmdlet and its settings properties. The APIs are deprecated and unsupported, which should be distinguished from undocumented; the roadmap facts, licensing background and console path are supported.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The console path is Teams Admin Settings > Meetings > Show meeting names.
claims.quote: On a Teams Rooms on Android device, open Teams Admin Settings > Meetings and toggle Show meeting names to Off to hide meeting names on the Teams Rooms device.

claims.claim: Show meeting names controls whether meeting names are visible on the room device.
claims.quote: For privacy purposes, meeting names can be hidden from Teams Rooms (Windows and Android) calendar and replaced with the organizer name if desired

claims.claim: Require passcode for all meetings is under Teams Admin Settings > Meetings on Teams Rooms on Android.
claims.quote: On Teams Rooms on Android devices, open Teams Admin Settings > Meetings and toggle Require passcode for all meetings to On to require room users to enter the meeting credentials to join all scheduled Teams meetings.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Rooms > device > Settings in the Teams Rooms Pro Management portal reaches the device settings page.
claims.quote: Go to Rooms/ Phones in the left navigation and click the device you want to configure. Select the Settings tab in the device panel.
claims.fix: The path correctly reaches the settings page but stops before the category and setting. Use 'Rooms > device > Settings > category > setting', with category and setting as placeholders, and retain the note listing the documented categories at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/rooms/pro-portal-settings.

claims.claim: Configuring device settings in the portal requires Rooms Management role-based access control permissions.
claims.quote: provided you have the necessary role-based access control permissions for Rooms Management.

claims.claim: Portal settings management is available only for signed-in devices.
claims.quote: Settings management is available only for signed-in devices. Ensure that the device is signed in for settings changes from the Teams Rooms Pro management portal to be applied successfully.

claims.claim: The device Settings tab has categories including About, Account, Meetings, Device and Network.
claims.quote: Use the left navigation in the device panels to browse settings categories (About, Account, Meetings, Device, Network, etc.).

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Settings changed directly on the device synchronise back to the portal and appear in its Settings tab.
claims.quote: Any setting changes made directly on the device are synchronized back to the Teams Rooms Pro Management portal and reflected in the Settings tab of the device panel, providing visibility into the device's current configuration.

claims.claim: The Graph beta teamworkDevice management APIs are deprecated and unsupported after November 2025.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Graph beta APIs related to device management under the teamworkDevice resource type will be deprecated by November 2025 and will no longer be supported after that date.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: remote settings automation cell
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automation for changing room device settings remotely.
claims.quote:
Update the navigation property configuration in teamwork
Update-MgBetaTeamworkDeviceConfiguration
-TeamworkDeviceId <string>
[-TeamsClientConfiguration <IMicrosoftGraphTeamworkTeamsClientConfiguration>]
claims.fix: Replace the null API side with kind 'powershell', call 'Update-MgBetaTeamworkDeviceConfiguration -TeamworkDeviceId <device-id> -TeamsClientConfiguration <teams-client-configuration>', and the cited cmdlet reference as docs. Keep an explicit note: 'Historical documentation only: the underlying Graph beta device-management APIs are unsupported after November 2025; do not use this as supported automation for the redesign.' Deprecated documentation is not an absence of documentation.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: meeting settings automation cell
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automation for the meeting-name visibility setting.
claims.quote:
TEAMSCLIENTCONFIGURATION <IMicrosoftGraphTeamworkTeamsClientConfiguration>
[FeaturesConfiguration <IMicrosoftGraphTeamworkFeaturesConfiguration>]
[IsHideMeetingNamesEnabled <Boolean?>]: True if hiding meeting names is enabled.
claims.fix: Replace the null API side with kind 'powershell', call 'Update-MgBetaTeamworkDeviceConfiguration -TeamworkDeviceId <device-id> -TeamsClientConfiguration @{ FeaturesConfiguration = @{ IsHideMeetingNamesEnabled = $true } }', and the cited cmdlet reference as docs. Retain the Pro-only licence note and state: 'Historical documentation only: the underlying Graph beta APIs are unsupported after November 2025; this is not supported automation for the redesign.'

claims.claim: The deprecated Graph device-management API is not supported automation for this redesign.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Graph beta APIs related to device management under the teamworkDevice resource type will be deprecated by November 2025 and will no longer be supported after that date.
